about: Born, Not Made, simplified version after the sketch of 21 November 2026. Frame: x toward the opening, y port, z up, meters; origin on the docking plane, on the inner floor (the tank floor is 3 mm lower).

stages.name: Dock
stages.text: The tail docks to the gel chamber from above: the rack of the tail reaches over the bowl, and three disc magnets close the thin docking ring.

stages.name: Unfold, gel
stages.text: The arm unfolds and injects the gel: 2.9 L at 0.1 L per minute. This is the first fill; the gel then stays in the bowl from birth to birth. Then the water comes in.

stages.name: Kit
stages.text: The electromagnet picks the electronics kit once, from the store in the tail, and places the kit in the gel, before any printing.

stages.name: Tool change
stages.text: One tool change at the rack in the tail: holder off, print needle on (Rotrics quick release).

stages.name: Print
stages.text: The DexArm prints the folded newborn around the kit: 44 m of bead, 0.08 L of Dragon Skin 10 NV.

stages.name: Cure, change
stages.text: Cure, and the second tool change: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Air in, nose up
stages.text: The ball needle enters the valve. Air pushes the trapped gel out of the folds, the newborn floats up in the gel, and the arm presses the tail end down so the nose rises above the lip.

stages.name: Push while inflating
stages.text: The arm steers the tail end from above and pushes; the newborn slides over the lip, and each segment opens outside. No contractions.

stages.name: Hold and fill
stages.text: The arm holds, the newborn fills to full size, the needle lets go.

stages.name: Float
stages.text: The newborn floats in the water: gravity, buoyancy, drag, a damped settling.

stages.name: Swim
stages.text: The newborn takes ballast, sits lower and swims on two jets.

notes: The tail is lowered onto the tank floor behind the gel chamber; the tools on the rack and the kit in the cradle go down into the wells and the neck of the bowl. Three magnets close the dry seam.
The arm unfolds out of the tail, between the two parked modules, over the gel bowl. The base does not move.
Gel comes through the line on the arm; the arm moves the outlet over three fill points.
With the gel in, the tank is filled with water to 93 mm. The gel stands higher than the water at the seam.
The bare arm folds back between the two parked modules in the tail.
The bare arm turns in behind the holder: an electromagnet and a ball needle.
The quick release slides onto the holder and clicks.
The holder slides forward out of the fork.
The holder moves along the narrow well to the kit store, in the neck on the centerline of the tail.
The needle goes down into the well of the kit; the magnet lands on the steel disk.
Magnet on: the magnet holds the kit by the steel disk.
The kit is carried forward through the gel and up, out of the tail, over the print seat.
The kit goes straight down through the gel onto the three seat bumps.
Magnet off: the kit stays on the seat, held by the gel; the holder lifts clear.
Tool change in the tail: the holder goes back through the neck.
The holder goes back into the fork, along the narrow well.
The pin on the fork presses the release; the module stays.
The bare arm turns 48 degrees, behind the modules, to the print needle.
The quick release clicks onto the print needle.
The needle slides forward out of the fork, through the gel.
The needle goes forward through the gel to the kit.
The folded newborn is printed around the kit, layer by layer, in clear silicone.
The silicone cures in the gel (75 minutes at room temperature). The print needle goes back to the rack in the tail.
The holder is back on the arm: the ball needle beside the magnet now carries the air.
The ball needle goes to the valve on the tail end of the newborn.
Air at 450 Pa pushes the gel out of the folds through the vent in the nose; the drained newborn rises 29 mm and floats in the gel.
The needle presses the tail end down in the gel: the nose rises above the lip of the opening.
Push while inflating: every segment opens once the segment is out of the opening. All the air comes through the ball needle on the arm.
At full reach the arm holds the needle in the valve while the rest of the air goes in; the skin stretches by a quarter and the creases pull smooth.
The needle lets go. The newborn floats free, rocks and settles; the arm parks the module and folds back into the tail.
The kit pumps take water into the belly pocket until the jets are under water; the newborn swims a slow turn on two jets.

checks.name: Tail prints in one piece on the H2S: 336 x 314 x 336 mm of 340 x 320 x 340
Head with the mouth and the ramp prints in one piece: 316 x 314 x 336 mm; the separate mouth piece is not needed
Folded arm ends 6 mm behind the docking plane; tower top 11 mm under the tail roof
Rack and kit cradle are arms of the tail print: they reach 55 mm forward of the docking plane, over the bowl of the head, with the forks 4 mm above the gel; the head carries no rack and no shelf
The print needle reaches all 1440 sampled print points inside the official joint ranges

The parts dock and take the gel in the dry tank. With the gel in and 93 mm of water, the tail weighs 6.1 kg against 5.7 kg of buoyancy (with the 5 mm steel plate under the arm base and 0.74 kg of extra steel)
The filled gel chamber rests on the floor: weight 4.4 kg, buoyancy 3.7 kg
Without gel the parts would lift in the water (together 7.8 kg against 9.4 kg of buoyancy), so the gel goes in before the water, and the bowl is not emptied under water

The lip of the mouth is 17 mm above the water and 3 mm above the gel. The docking seam is dry: the whole bowl, with the neck and the two wells, is in the head print, and the rear wall of the neck stands 4 mm ahead of the docking plane
The gel stays in the bowl between births: 2.91 L in the bowl, about 19 mL leave with each newborn (0.6 percent); the level falls 0.6 mm a birth, topped up through the arm
The lip is 3 mm above the gel surface; the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm, and the folded print has already raised the level before the push
All parts sit at the tail end, behind a printed bulkhead 72 mm behind the arm axis, inside the taper; the nearest a part comes to the shell is 5.3 mm
Energy for one cycle about 25 Wh (the Raspberry Pi 5 takes a third); the battery (six 18650 cells) holds 54 Wh: margin 2.1. The inflator runs on a battery of its own
Silicone: the two bores hold 119 mL, one newborn takes 83 mL

Air: the inflator of the artist fills a size 7 basketball (7.6 L, 55 kPa) in 35 s, which is 7.1 L of free air per minute; the newborn (11.2 L at 1.3 kPa) fills in about 95 s. The inflator must stop at 1.3 kPa: the preset of a tire inflator may not go that low (open question)
Every pose of the timeline is inside the official joint ranges (base -24 to 24, J1 0 to 55, J2 1 to 85 degrees)

Electromagnet (Adafruit 3872, 2.5 kg holding force): lifting force taken as a tenth, 2.5 N, through the thin silicone over the steel disk; the kit weighs 1.08 N in air and about 0.00 N in the gel: margin 2.3

Release in the gel: with the magnet off, the yield stress of the gel holds the seated kit with about 0.19 N; a remanent pull of 2 percent would be 0.05 N (estimate; a short reverse pulse makes the release certain)
The steel disk adds 2.5 g on top of the kit; the metacentric height with ballast stays 62 mm
Payload while carrying the kit: 193 g of 500 g
Force of the needle on the valve stays under the payload: peak 1.76 N of 4.91 N
The rubber ball valve grips the needle against the largest upward pull: 1.33 N of about 2 N (estimate, to bench test)
The newborn leaves through the center of the opening: in the middle of the push the axis of the body crosses the face 20 mm from the center of the 134 x 156 mm opening
Folds can be printed: story pitch 3.6 mm with one valley, pleat walls 7.1 mm apart at mid depth (limit: 1.2 mm wall plus 2 mm of gel)
Kresling stories are bistable with a barrier strain of 2.2 percent, far under the 25 percent stretch of the skin
Stretch 1.25 stays under the limit point of the membrane (1.38) and uses 4 percent of the 663 percent elongation at break
Full size 428 x 301 mm against the gel chamber 243 x 314 x 336 mm: 176 percent of the length, 96 percent of the width
The newborn floats upright: metacentric height 39 mm dry, 62 mm with ballast
Draft 38 mm dry; 0.14 kg of water in the belly pocket puts the jets 45 mm under water
The motion settles: pitch rate in the last three seconds under 0.03 degrees per second; deepest contact at the lip 0.14 mm
Per frame penetration test over 2380 frames: deepest overlap of any pair 0.78 mm (limit 1 mm)
UNS 150U: the parent body (597 mm long, 336 mm tall) and the newborn (428 mm) in the 1470 mm inner length, with a swim run of 639 mm; water 68 L, about 203 kg filled

deriv.name: Arm base
deriv.value: fixed, 103 mm behind the docking plane, on a 5 mm steel plate on the tail floor
deriv.why: The folded DexArm reaches 97 mm ahead of its axis. Ahead of the folded arm the tail needs 6 mm more for the rack: the modules hang 150 mm ahead of the axis, the nearest the arm can hold a tool. From there the tool tip reaches 393 mm from the axis at the height of the print.

deriv.name: Tail
deriv.value: 278 mm long from the docking plane to the point, 19.8 L; print 336 x 314 x 336 mm with the rack
deriv.why: The arm stands at the very front: axis 103 mm behind the docking plane, the base plate 25 mm behind the plane. Right behind the arm tower the tail runs to a point: the roof falls from 45 mm ahead of the arm axis, the sides close from 55 mm ahead of the axis, the floor rises from 65 mm behind the axis, each on a convex curve (an ellipse quarter), to one rounded point at mid height 175 mm behind the axis. The curves are the furthest forward that keep 5 mm to the folded arm (314 mm tall on its plate) and 3 mm to the parts at the tail end; over the whole timeline the arm comes no nearer than 5 mm. The tail holds 19.8 L (round 4: 23.1 L). Shell length 278 mm (round 4: 272 mm from the plane to the point); the rack reaches 55 mm further forward, so the print is 336 mm long, 4, 6 and 4 mm clear of the H2S.

deriv.name: Print needle
deriv.why: The head stays above the gel (92 mm deep over the lowest printed point) while the tip prints the lowest layer.

deriv.name: Printed newborn
deriv.why: With the needle hanging 122 mm below the wrist, the arm reaches from 206 mm to 393 mm from its axis at the axis of the print, and from 237 mm to 371 mm at the top of the print. The 150 mm body lies from 221 mm to 371 mm. The 90 mm diameter is the smallest that holds the kit on the belly.

deriv.name: Full size newborn
deriv.why: The skin that packs into the folded volume at the packing of the full size study (silicone 47 percent of the folded volume): 0.170 m2. Kresling stories (n = 16, twist 14.3 degrees a story) open the length, sixteen star pleats open the girth, a 25 percent stretch pulls the creases smooth. Unfolding at about 300 Pa (estimate), full at 1251 Pa.

deriv.name: Shape of the newborn
deriv.value: one smooth spindle, widest at 62 percent of the length
deriv.why: Eight segments between nine rings follow one curve: a blunt tail end of 38 mm radius with the valve, a long taper, the widest ring (151 mm radius), a shorter taper to the nose. At full reach the valve is 98 mm short of the lip, so the ring that stands in the opening while the last air goes in is 52 mm in radius; that ring sets the size of the opening.

deriv.name: Gel bowl
deriv.value: 2.91 L of gel, flat surface at 104 mm
deriv.why: The bowl lies in the head alone. Its floor is flat; its front is one straight ramp at 62.0 degrees that starts 347 mm from the arm axis, under the tapered nose of the folded print (ring radii 45, 41, 35, 26 mm, with 4 mm of gel under each), and reaches the height of the lip after 57 mm; the lip then runs out 12 mm as the lower jaw of the mouth. The ramp is as flat as the mouth allows: a flatter ramp moves the lip away from the arm, a wider ring of the newborn then stands in the mouth during the last fill, and the opening would grow until the body no longer leaves through its center (45 degrees needs an opening 184 mm tall, with the body 42 mm below the center). Behind the bowl, up to the docking plane, the head has a terrace at rim height with one neck 68 mm wide for the kit and two narrow wells for the tool stems: 0.59 L of the total.

deriv.name: Docking plane
deriv.value: 103 mm ahead of the arm axis, a thin 4 mm ring, three magnets, dry
deriv.why: The plane stands right ahead of the arm: the folded arm ends 6 mm behind the plane, the base plate 25 mm. The seam is dry and carries no seal: no gel touches the seam, the rear wall of the neck is 4 mm ahead of the plane, and the plane is closed below the rim by the rear wall of the head. This works because the rack and the kit cradle are arms of the tail print that reach forward over the bowl, so the tools hang with their stems in the wells of the head and no tool crosses a wall. The price: the tail docks from above (the stems and the kit go down into the wells and the neck), not by sliding along the floor. Three DC2-N52 disc magnets on steel discs hold 161 N.

deriv.name: Rack and kit store
deriv.value: arms of the tail print, 150 mm ahead of the arm axis, 24 degrees to each side
deriv.why: Close to its base the DexArm holds the wrist at 134 mm and no higher, so a module hangs with the head 112 mm above the floor, the ball needle of the holder at 57 mm and the print needle tip at 12 mm. No wall can stand between such a tool and the print, so the tools hang over the bowl, stems in two narrow wells of the head (gel surface 104 mm). The forks, 4 mm above the gel, are carried by thin beams that run back to a cross beam on the tail wall just behind the docking plane; the kit waits in a cradle that hangs from the same beams into the neck, on the centerline. The bare quick release comes up behind a module (33 mm of travel), clicks on, and slides the module forward out of the fork. The arm folds and unfolds through the 74 mm between the two parked heads. Variants that failed: a rack beside the arm (base turned 90 degrees) needs wells 144 mm long that cross the seam, which makes the seam wet; lifting a tool over the rim needs the tool 243 mm from the axis, outside the tail when turned to the side; a raised base does not fit under the 336 mm roof.

deriv.name: Opening
deriv.value: an ellipse of 134 x 156 mm standing on the lip, in a front face that leans back 8 degrees; lip 416 mm from the arm axis, 107 mm high
deriv.why: The lip continues the line of the gel surface, as drawn: 3 mm above the gel (the yield stress of the gel holds a crest of about 2.5 mm) and 17 mm above the water. The opening is only as large as the passing body needs: the folded body is 90 mm across, the ring that stands in the opening during the last fill is 104 mm across, and the body crosses the face at a pitch. The center of the opening lies on the push axis (20 mm apart in the middle of the push). The rest of the front is closed, part of the gel chamber print. The face leans only 8 degrees: the module head of the print needle works right behind the face when the top layers of the nose are printed, and a face that leaned further would cut through the head.

deriv.name: Head (gel chamber)
deriv.value: 316 x 314 x 336 mm outside, one print, a bare shell
deriv.why: With the arm moved forward the head, with the mouth and the ramp, is 316 mm long and still fits the H2S in one piece, 24 mm clear. The cut for a separate mouth piece is therefore not needed; if a longer mouth is wanted later, the cut would stand 343 mm from the arm axis, at the foot of the ramp, and the mouth piece would be 76 x 307 x 314 mm. That joint would lie under the gel and the water line and would be bonded and sealed. The head carries the bowl with the neck and the wells, the ramp, the mouth and three seat bumps, nothing to fit afterwards.

deriv.name: Water
deriv.why: Deep enough for the newborn with ballast (draft 45 mm) with 48 mm under the belly; low enough to stay 17 mm under the lip and 14 mm under the gel.

deriv.name: Time
deriv.why: First gel fill 29 min at 0.1 L per minute (micro peristaltic pump; later cycles only top up), print 43 min for 44 m of bead at 20 mm per second, cure 75 min, air about 95 s for 11.2 L: the inflator adds 55 kPa to a 7.6 L basketball in 35 s, so 7.6 x 55 / 101 = 4.1 L of free air in 35 s, 7.1 L per minute.

deriv.name: Tail contents
deriv.value: 6 parts, 0.75 kg, at the tail end
deriv.why: Cut to what one cycle needs, with the parts of the artist. Air: the CaRSun cordless inflator, 75 x 60 x 32 mm, with a battery of its own. Controller: the Raspberry Pi 5. Battery for the arm, the controller and the small pumps: about 25 Wh a cycle (arm 12 W while moving, estimate), six 18650 cells hold 54 Wh. Gel: one micro peristaltic pump; no gel store, the gel stays in the bowl. Silicone: two bores of the print with pistons, 119 mL for the 83 mL of one newborn. The kit is picked by a 5 V electromagnet (20 mm, 22.7 g) on the holder, switched by the Raspberry Pi 5, on a steel disk on top of the kit: no vacuum system. The newborn carries a ball inflation valve; the ball inflation needle stands beside the magnet on the holder, with the three way stopcock on the arm, set by hand before the cycle. The two FIT0800 water pumps stay in the kit of the newborn. All of these sit at the tail end behind a thin printed bulkhead, inside the taper, on printed seats.

deriv.name: Printing the two parts
deriv.why: Tail: 336 x 314 x 336 mm in print orientation, about 1.2 kg of clear PETG at a 3 mm wall with the bulkhead and the rack, about 15 h at 18 mm3 per second. Gel chamber: 316 x 314 x 336 mm, about 1.6 kg, about 20 h. Both stand on the docking face, so the domes close without tall supports; the rack forks and the kit shelf need supports that break off. The fallback is not needed: each part in two blocks, split on the horizontal plane at half height, with a 6 mm tongue and groove and a solvent weld.

verdict.point: Two printed parts, tail and head, each in one piece on the H2S; a third mouth piece allowed
verdict.ok: yes, two prints, the third is not needed
verdict.why: Tail 336 x 314 x 336 mm with the rack, head 316 x 314 x 336 mm with mouth and ramp, against 340 x 320 x 340 mm.

verdict.point: Docking seam at the arm tower, dry
verdict.why: The plane stands 103 mm ahead of the arm axis, 25 mm ahead of the base plate. The seam is dry and has no seal. Three disc magnets, 161 N, on a 4 mm ring.

verdict.point: The shell of the gel chamber holds the gel in its lower part
verdict.why: 2.91 L, surface at 104 mm, in one small bowl with a ramp to the lip.

verdict.point: The arm at the very front of the tail, on a fixed base; folds back, unfolds to work
verdict.why: Axis 103 mm behind the docking plane; the folded arm ends 6 mm behind the plane; all 2380 poses of the timeline are inside the joint ranges.

verdict.point: The arm as drawn: a tower, then two long links over the top of the docking face
verdict.why: The tower of the DexArm already contains the upper arm: the shoulder is 127 mm above the base and each link is 150 mm. The wrist reaches 282 mm above the floor at most, and only close to the base; at the far end of the print the wrist is at 211 mm.

verdict.point: One opening, on a slant at the upper front, thin plain rim, no magnets
verdict.ok: yes, lower, smaller and less slanted than drawn
verdict.why: An ellipse of 134 x 156 mm standing on the lip (107 mm high, on the line of the gel surface), in a face leaning back 8 degrees (a steeper slant would cut through the module head while the nose is printed). The ball needle on the fixed arm reaches 186 mm high at 318 mm from the axis and no further, so the opening has to come to the arm.

verdict.point: All equipment at the tail end, behind the arm
verdict.why: 0.75 kg of parts (battery 54 Wh, the inflator, the Raspberry Pi 5, a micro gel pump, two silicone bores with their drive) sit between 72 mm and 157 mm behind the arm axis, inside the taper.

verdict.point: Gel bowl as drawn in orange: flat top that runs on as the lip
verdict.why: The lip is 3 mm above the gel surface and 17 mm above the water.

verdict.point: Flat gel surface, about 3 L or less
verdict.why: 2.91 L, surface at 104 mm, of which 0.59 L in the neck and the two wells.

verdict.point: A mouth that sticks out, with one long flat ramp down to the bowl floor
verdict.why: The head narrows to a mouth of 134 x 156 mm whose lower lip runs out 12 mm; the ramp is straight, 62.0 degrees over 57 mm. As long and flat as drawn (about 30 to 45 degrees) does not hold: the ball needle reaches no further than 334 mm from the arm axis at the height of the valve, so a lip further out leaves a wider ring of the newborn in the mouth during the last fill; at 45 degrees the mouth would have to be 184 mm tall and the body would pass 42 mm below its center.

verdict.point: The tail tapers to a real point right behind the arm tower
verdict.why: Roof, sides and floor run on convex curves from the arm to one rounded point 175 mm behind the arm axis. Volume 19.8 L (round 4: 23.1 L). The taper cannot start further forward: the folded arm is 314 mm tall and 184 mm wide at the turntable.

verdict.point: Tool modules, tool changes and the kit store in the tail, a bare head
verdict.ok: yes, as arms of the tail print
verdict.why: Rack and kit cradle are printed with the tail and reach 55 mm forward of the docking plane, over the bowl. The head print carries no rack, no shelf and no insert. The tail therefore docks from above.

verdict.point: The parent body rests on the tank floor; only the newborn floats
verdict.why: In 93 mm of water the tail weighs 6.1 kg (with steel ballast under the arm base where needed) against 5.7 kg of buoyancy, the filled gel chamber 4.4 kg against 3.7 kg; the empty gel chamber is held down by the docked tail.

verdict.point: The newborn grows to about the size of the gel chamber
verdict.why: Printed 150 x 90 mm, full size 428 x 301 mm: 176 percent of the length and 96 percent of the width of the gel chamber, 72 percent of the length of the whole parent body. The limit is the skin that packs into a print the arm can reach.

verdict.point: Birth by pushing while inflating, all air through the arm
verdict.why: The needle steers the tail end from above; the body slides over the lip; peak force 1.76 N of 4.91 N. A vertical tool cannot pull the body up a ramp, so the gel carries the body inside and the lip and the water carry the body outside.

limits: Open points on the parts: a tire inflator may not stop as low as 1.3 kPa; the force of the electromagnet through the silicone skin and its release in the gel need a bench test; the product pages of the inflator, the stopcock and the ball valve were read by the artist and the coordinator, not opened from here.

Estimates, to measure: the mass of the DexArm (2.4 kg), the power of the DexArm while moving (12 W), the mass of the inflator, the size of the micro pumps beyond the published figures, the module head (30 x 40 x 52 mm), the seal of the cup, the flow of gel through a 3.5 mm tube, the pressure that opens the folds (300 Pa), the yield stress of the gel (25 Pa), the pump curve of the kit pumps, friction at the lip (0.2).

How the official joint angles J1 and J2 map onto the link meshes is an assumption, as on the full version. The DexArm specification page could not be opened again from here on 21 November 2026; its numbers are those used on the full version.

The valve is a soft boss on the tail cap and the nozzle stays vertical while the body pitches by up to 36 degrees: this needs a bench test. So does the drain of the gel from the folds, and whether a fold packed this tightly prints and opens as drawn.
The force on the valve is a quasi static estimate from slices: weight, buoyancy in the gel and in the water, the lip with friction, yield drag.

The newborn is drawn rigid with one soft droop where the body leaves the opening; a real skin at 300 Pa also wrinkles. In the force estimate the unfolded part outside is limp at that droop: the lip, the hull front and the water carry that part, and the arm steers only the part still inside. Friction at the gel wet lip is taken as 0.2.
The swim is a straight run on both jets and one slow turn; the speed comes from an estimated pump curve.
Overlap is measured from sampled points (4 to 11 mm apart) against exact surfaces, so a figure can be about 1 mm off.

read.birth_text: Quasi static estimate from slices. Peak 1.76 N; the payload of the DexArm is 4.91 N. The needle pushes forward and down; the gel carries the body inside, the lip and the water carry the body outside.
read.tank_text: The tank is the Ultum Nature Systems UNS 150U, a rimless low iron glass tank of 1500 x 600 x 600 mm with 15 mm glass (the longest stock length under 1.8 m; no stock tank is 1.3 m). The parent body, 597 mm long and 336 mm tall, stands on the floor at one end; 93 mm of water (68 L) leave the lip of the opening 17 mm above the water and give the newborn 769 mm of open water ahead. Filled as shown the tank weighs about 203 kg.
